summary: Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He served at Hiroshima University as an associate professor (~1989–1997) and later as a professor, including in the Department of Indian Philosophy (~1997–2020).

Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held posts there as assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Hilko Wiardo Schomerus (1879–1945) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig Mission, Kiel, and Leipzig, under Paul Deussen and Nathan Söderblom. He held posts at Kiel University (1918–1923) and the University of Halle (~1925–1945).

Himal Trikha is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as an academic assistant in training at the University of Vienna (attested 2000–2009) and as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

Himanshu Prabha Ray specializes in Indology and archaeology. She studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she was an associate professor (1980–2012). She also held posts at National Monuments Authority, OCHS, and Munich.

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810) and served at the University of Breslau (~1813–1845).

Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia (b. 1894) specialized in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a teacher for Ph.D. students in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward studied at Harvard and Yale, working in archaeology and Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at Silpakorn, Michigan, and Vermont, and served as curator of Asian art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at DAV College and Oriental College. He held posts at DAV College, Panjab University, the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, and Baroda State (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda (b. 1938) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He held lecturer and associate professor posts at Tohoku University and is an emeritus professor at Shimane University.

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami (~1959–1965). He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1974–2000) and was a special member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. She held an appointment as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Hiroshima University (B.A.) and Leipzig University (Dr. phil.), and has held research positions at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023), and the University of Vienna (2024).

Hiromasa Tosaki (1930–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and Harvard under multiple scholars, later teaching at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College and serving as a professor at Kyushu University (~1978–1993).

Hiromi Habata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held academic posts at Ryukoku University, including as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987 and 2006).
Hiromichi Kato (b. 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Ryogon Fukuhara as a graduate student and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Hiromitsu Ikuma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Tohoku University by 2019. He has served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2020) and at the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies.
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1944–1949) and later served there as a professor (~1969–1995).

Hironori Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020). He held a post at Bukkyo University and is attested as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
